step_1_findings.terminal_is_self_contained: cells/apps/terminal (3471028bc worktree /tmp/cellbox-s10-7/worktree): TerminalSession::execute_command interprets help/clear/uname/pwd/ls/ps/date/echo/exit in-process; every other word prints `shell: command not found: <name>`. It does NOT embed /bin/shell, does NOT spawn it (the manifest declares spawn=true but the source never calls a spawn syscall) and has no exit status. `ls` prints a fixed string regardless of argument, `ps` a fixed 9-row table, `cat` does not exist, `echo` joins its arguments. Compiled bytes verified: the signed /bin/terminal (sha a7d6926f...) contains the banner, the fixed ls string, `shell: command not found: ` and no `/bin/shell` path.

Single-reader stream lease active.`, empty row, `Cellos > ` with the cursor at cell (9, 3) (the Cellbox terminal shows an empty row, its own banner and the prompt with the cursor at (9, 2)).

step_1_findings.drivable_with_existing_machinery: YES, without a new oracle: the retained Proof/Desk pixel oracle, InputGate, TemporalDesk, SerializedTraceControl, AtomicClient, coordinated observer/surface, B2 fingerprint/memory observer and status helpers are reused unchanged. What differs: (a) the EXPECTED rows are the B2 terminal's source literals (initial screen, ls/ps/cat/echo outputs) instead of the Cellbox banner and Cellbox outputs; (b) no status epoch (`echo st=$?` prints the literal text; no `$?` exists) - command completion is judged by the retained exact-screen Desk.command (exact typed line, exact output screen, one-character and previous-frame negative controls); (c) no recovery waits (no cancellable command); (d) the memory focus is the terminal task (64-page stacks), the shell is a second measured task; (e) no Cellbox heapwatch, so no allocator peak.
step_1_findings.stop_condition_not_met: the B2 terminal is drivable and observable with the existing real-GUI machinery without inventing a new oracle, so the run was prepared; the row is null only if the run fails.

disclosed_deviations_and_ceilings: B2 desktop shared subset is the B2 GUI terminal's in-process builtins with fixed outputs: `ls /` and `ps` are canned strings, `cat` does not exist (exact expected output is `shell: command not found: cat`), there is no exit status; none of the five shared commands exercises VFS, spawn or a process list. This is the real B2 desktop behaviour, recorded as such.
Status via select_status is NOT applicable (no st= row can exist); its fail-closed behaviour on the expected B2 rows is proven offline only. Completion = exact-screen oracle.

Boot medium is the retained ISO cdrom argv (read from a private copy) with 256M, one vCPU, restricted user netdev; the v2 boot smokes used the qcow2 virtio disk with 2048M and -smp 2. The v2 image has never booted on this argv before this run (same risk class as S10-7 disclosed for the b2-headless/candidate sets); the ISO's boot structure and kernel were checked statically.
The NVMe data disk of the retained argv is dropped (B2 needs no data disk; the smoke booted without one).

Only terminal and shell are memory-measured (compositor, desktop, vfs and the rest are not); stack depths are lower-bound sentinel depths on a hooks measurement kernel (not the promoted kernel), regions are mapped-backed under eager SAS, all guest numbers are QEMU/TCG.

The image is non-pristine (S10-9.3: services rebuilt from source at the commit, unsigned/tracked fixtures and a few historical bytes kept) and a historical comparator only; nothing here claims CBX-27 or Phase 10 criterion 4 is met.
